name: נגזרת של e^(θ·cos θ) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:

\( \displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[ {{CT:1}}\right] = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Use the chain rule for the exponential; the derivative of the exponent needs the product rule.
Step 1 — The chain rule
To solve this problem you will need to use the product rule and the chain rule.
The product rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv' \)
The chain rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\,g'(x) \)
Let \(g({{CT:0}})={{CT:2}}\) and \(f({{CT:0}})=e^{g({{CT:0}})}\). Then,

\[ \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] = \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}. \]

Step 2 — The inner function: the product rule
In order to calculate \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you need to use the product rule, by defining two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:0}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}}\) so that \(g({{CT:0}})=h({{CT:0}})i({{CT:0}})\). So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:2}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i + h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle [{{CT:4}}]{{CT:3}} + {{CT:0}}[{{CT:5}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}} \end{array} \]

Step 3 — Putting it together
Hence,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}(e^g) \cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:2}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle e^{{CT:2}} \cdot ({{CT:6}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}} \end{array} \]
